digo: Mvundza jembe; Mvundza kondo (also Mbanda tchitswa, Muvudza kondo)
digo_source: Pakia (2005) App. III; Pakia (2005) App. VI; Maundu & Tengnäs 2005 (under Allophylus africanus)

teaser.en: Its name means 'hoe breaker', and it plays a part in rites that bring an end to quarrels in families and villages.

summary.en: *Mvundza jembe* is a variable bush shrub with three-part toothed leaves and small red berries. It is a ritual medicine for settling disputes, and a medicine to 'end the war with disease in the body'.

about.en: *Mvundza jembe* is a very variable shrub, sometimes upright, sometimes scrambling. Each leaf has three toothed leaflets, a little like a bramble leaf. It bears small berries that ripen red.

where.en: It grows in bushland and on forest edges.

uses.en: It is used as a ritual medicine for settling disputes, and as a medicine 'to end the war with disease in the body'.

culture.en: *Mvundza jembe* means 'hoe breaker'. It is used in rites that end domestic and community disputes, in which a hoe serves as a symbolic item. Its other name, *mvundza kondo*, means 'breaker of war', and the same idea runs through its medicinal use: ending a war, whether between people or inside the body.

names.en: Pakia records *mvundza jembe* and *mvundza kondo*; other recorded forms are *mbanda tchitswa* and *muvudza kondo*. ICRAF records its names under a related species, *Allophylus africanus*. In Swahili it is *mlishangwa* or *mkona chuma*, and in Giriama *munyanga kitswa*. No English common name has been recorded.

sources: Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: an ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD thesis, Univ. Bayreuth, Appendix III (Digo–botanical name list) & Appendix VI (name semantics). https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf
Maundu, P. & Tengnäs, B. (eds) (2005) Useful Trees and Shrubs for Kenya, ICRAF — sheet Allophylus africanus: https://apps.worldagroforestry.org/usefultrees/pdflib/Allophylus_africanus_KEN.pdf
